Not a figure published pre-computed by WSC. Most recent years may be provisional. Not at the mouth: Hope is upstream of the mouth, but is the long-record gauge on the lower main stem; flow added below Hope is not included (gauge area 216,600 km2 vs 228,100 km2 at Mission). Includes the Thompson. Mission (08MH024, tidal reach, 228,100 km2) is further down but has only 27 complete years (1966–1992) and gives 3,340 m3/s; see alternates.

flow.caveat: Mean = average of annual means over complete calendar years only (every day present), computed from WSC daily mean discharge via the ECCC open-data API (cross-checked against monthly means, within 0.5%). Not a figure published pre-computed by WSC. Most recent years may be provisional. Downstream-most Canadian main-stem gauge, at the US border; not at the mouth (Pacific), so flow added in the US is not included. Its drainage area (155,200 km2) is much larger than Birchbank's (87,390 km2); the difference matches the Pend d'Oreille (65,640 km2 at the boundary, station 08NE119), which appears to join above this gauge (inference from gauge areas). Includes the Kootenay (joins at Castlegar, above the gauge) and excludes the Okanagan (joins in Washington). Record ends 2021 in the data feed. Flow regulated by dams (general knowledge).

flow.caveat: Mean = average of annual means over complete calendar years only (every day present), computed from WSC daily mean discharge via the ECCC open-data API (cross-checked against monthly means, within 0.5%). Not a figure published pre-computed by WSC. Most recent years may be provisional. Downstream-most long-record main-stem gauge, in Alberta (Wood Buffalo National Park); the Peace does not reach the sea, it flows on as the Slave River to the Mackenzie system, so this is near the end of the Peace, not 'a mouth'. Includes Alberta tributaries well beyond the BC portion (gauge area 299,400 km2). The BC gauge Peace River near Taylor (07FD002, 100,800 km2) gives 1,411 m3/s (1949–2024), see alternates. Flow regulated by W.A.C. Bennett Dam since the late 1960s (general knowledge).

flow.station: KOOTENAY LAKE OUTFLOW NEAR CORRA LINN
flow.caveat: Mean = average of annual means over complete calendar years only (every day present), computed from WSC daily mean discharge via the ECCC open-data API (cross-checked against monthly means, within 0.5%). Not a figure published pre-computed by WSC. Most recent years may be provisional. Not at the mouth (confluence with the Columbia is downstream): this is the outflow of Kootenay Lake and excludes the Slocan River and other inflows below it. The Kootenay passes through the US (Montana/Idaho) upstream of this gauge, so the gauge integrates that flow. Flow is regulated by upstream dams (general knowledge). Data series begins 1937 under this station ID; WSC may have merged predecessor records. Kootenay is part of the Columbia basin, so do not add it to the Columbia.

Not a figure published pre-computed by WSC. Most recent years may be provisional. Border-side gauge: downstream-most Canadian main-stem gauge, above Osoyoos Lake and the US border; the river continues in Washington State to the Columbia and flow added there is not included. Does not represent the mouth. Heavily regulated and used for irrigation. Note the very small flow (about 19 m3/s) compared with the other nine.
